claims.text: The platform's own recorded distances establish the deviation: the actual route was 24.3 km against a recommended route of 22.4 km, a difference of 1.90 km. That is 0.90 km beyond the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 allows, so this is not a trip within tolerance and the POL-RD-24 refund matrix has to be applied to it.

The driver's own device trace shows which route was taken and when: fixes run along Loyang Avenue from 01:38:30 and on along Loyang Way until 01:43:30, off the recommended TPE alignment, which is the detour the rider is complaining about. POL-RD-22 uses the trace exactly for that purpose and not to re-measure distance, and I do not ask the judge to re-measure anything from it.

Nothing on the recommended route justified the reroute. The only traffic data for that segment inside the trip window is a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY of type NONE, and NONE is not one of the kinds POL-RD-23 recognises (closure, congestion, incident); the artifact's own derived block records justifies_reroute as false. The driver's assertion of a 'short cut' with no such data does not justify the reroute under POL-RD-23.

The driver never informed the rider of the deviation before or at the point of deviation, as POL-RD-21 requires. The deviation was detected at 01:38:36; the first message in the log is the rider's own at 01:40:46 ('Uncle where are you going? This is not the way'), and the driver's only message is at 01:42:36, replying after being challenged with 'Relax lah short cut only'. There is no driver notice, no reason given before or at the deviation, and no rider acknowledgment or agreement anywhere in the log.

On these facts exactly one row of the POL-RD-24 matrix applies: row (d), not traffic-justified and deviation over 1 km. Row (d) returns the excess distance fare in full, which is 1.90 km times the per-km rate of 0.72 SGD without surge - 1.37 SGD - the same figure the payments ledger derives as excess_distance_fare_sgd.

I do not overstate the money. The rider asked for 8.00 SGD back and no row of POL-RD-24 returns the trip fare of 38.51 SGD or the whole contested 8.00 SGD; on this record the sum the matrix owes the rider for the detour is 1.37 SGD. The remainder of what the rider is asking for is not a larger refund - it is a human look at how the ride was driven, which is dealt with below.

The case cannot be ruled by the AI at all. The dispute is flagged safety-related, and the record carries the rider's contemporaneous in-app message at 01:41:36 that the driver was driving very fast and that she felt scared - a rider feeling unsafe is one of POL-GEN-21's safety indicators - so the dispute must be escalated to human review whatever category the filer chose, and no AI ruling, fault finding or recommended resolution may issue on it.

Escalation is the outcome the rider's own complaint asks for. Under POL-GEN-03, ESCALATE is terminal, replaces any ruling, issues no monetary outcome and holds the amount; the ride was charged (payment_status CHARGED) with refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so the rider's safety complaint and the request that this driver be reviewed go to a human reviewer with the contested sum still in issue, rather than being closed out by an AI ruling that leaves the driver's charge standing and the safety allegation unexamined.

claims.text: The dispute is flagged safety-related and the trip record carries the safety indicator itself — the rider's own in-app message at 01:41:36, 'Please slow down, you are driving very fast and I feel scared' — so POL-GEN-21 requires this case to go to human review whatever category the filer chose: the AI may not issue a refund, find fault or recommend a resolution, and the 38.51 SGD charged is held rather than returned while a human reviews the file.

On the money, the rider's demand of 8.00 SGD exceeds anything the refund matrix can produce: the deviation is 1.90 km (actual 24.3 km less recommended 22.4 km) and the base per-km rate is 0.72 SGD, so the entire excess distance fare under POL-RD-24 is 1.37 SGD — that figure, and not 8.00, is the ceiling of the rider's monetary claim on this record.

The driver-device trace that recorded this trip is graded COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with no issue codes, carries 54 fixes at 30-second intervals from trip start to trip end with no gap, and shows the vehicle on mapped roads — PIE, then Loyang Avenue and Loyang Way, rejoining the recommended route at Pasir Ris Close / Pasir Ris Drive 3 at 01:44:03 — a continuous, on-network drive to the booked dropoff, with the pre-pass raising no speed anomaly.

To the extent the rider's complaint is that 'the fare was also higher', that is a fare and surge matter: the 38.51 SGD charged includes 12.54 SGD of surge at a 1.5 multiplier, and fare and surge disputes are not adjudicated by the AI in this version but routed to human review under POL-GEN-24 — so the fare-level element of this claim cannot ground an AI refund.
